atoms.text: Macedonia was a kingdom to the north of the Greek city-states. Its capital city was called Pella. For most of the history of ancient Greece, Macedonia was a relatively small kingdom.

King Philip II expanded Macedonia and defeated most of the Greek states in 338 BC. He let them stay free and respected their culture, but they were still forced do what Philip, and later his son Alexander, wanted.

Philip died in 336 BC, soon after his victory. Alexander became king and decided to conquer the Persian empire because the Greek states were worried about another invasion. He was able to do this by uniting the Greek armies under his control.

hint.text: A prophecy is a prediction of the future. The ancient Greeks considered them very important.

atoms.b: This is the Gordian Knot. A prophecy said that the person who ((++untied tangled)) it would rule all of Asia.

instruction.text: Trace the line to slice the knot.

feedback.finish: The story goes that when Alexander found the Gordian Knot, he simply cut it in two with his sword. This meant that he had fulfilled the prophecy and would rule Asia!

atoms.b: Alexander began his ((++conquest condiment)) of Asia in 334 BC.
He first defeated ((++Syria Sheffield)) and then conquered Egypt, where he founded the city of Alexandria.
Alexander finally achieved victory by defeating King Darius III of Persia in several ((++battles baths)).

feedback.finish: Alexander’s conquest ended when his soldiers refused to travel any further, stopping just before India. He died of a fever in 323 BC, at the age of 32.
